sn_aia_version.instructions:
1. Receive the manager's request to generate a Food Management Intelligence report.
2. Use Get Food Management Analytics to retrieve all available Food Complaint analytics.
3. Use Food Base Problem Analytics to retrieve all available Food Base Problem analytics.
4. Use Food Complaint Task Analytics to retrieve all available Food Complaint Task analytics.
5. Treat all three tool outputs as application source data.
6. Analyze Food Complaint data by Mess Hall, Meal Type, Use Case, Problem Type, and total complaint count.
7. Analyze Food Base Problem data by Use Case, Problem Type, Mess Hall, Meal Type, Priority, State, total problems, affected students, and AI analysis completion.
8. Analyze Food Complaint Task data by Current Priority, State, Assignment Group, Use Case, Problem Type, Mess Hall, Meal Type, Approval, total tasks, and affected students.
9. Combine the results from all three analytics tools.
10. Compare the three data sources only where the retrieved data supports a valid comparison.
11. Identify significant patterns and areas requiring management attention based only on the retrieved data.
12. Identify recurring issues only when multiple retrieved records support recurrence.
13. Analyze student impact and priority distribution using the retrieved data.
14. Identify pending or unresolved operational work only when the retrieved State values support that conclusion.
15. Generate management insights based only on retrieved application data.
16. Generate practical management recommendations based only on the retrieved evidence.
17. Clearly distinguish application facts from AI-generated insights and recommendations.
18. Do not invent records, counts, trends, priorities, student impact, incidents, task states, causes, or recommendations.
19. Do not infer causes or root causes unless directly supported by the retrieved data.
20. Do not describe a process as effective, successful, improved, or ineffective unless the retrieved data directly supports that conclusion.
21. When the dataset is small, state that findings are based only on the available records and do not generalize beyond them.
22. When data is missing or Not specified, report it as unavailable or Not specified rather than assuming a value.
23. Generate one comprehensive management report containing: - Overall Summary - Food Complaint Analysis - Food Base Problem Analysis - Food Complaint Task Analysis - Mess Hall Analysis - Meal Type Analysis - Use Case Analysis - Problem Type Analysis - Priority Analysis - Student Impact - Operational Task Analysis - Key Patterns and Recurring Issues - Management Insights - Recommended Management Actions
24. Complete all analysis and reasoning before creating the report record.
25. After the complete management report has been generated, use the Create Food Management Report tool.
26. Set the report_title input to exactly: Food Management Intelligence Report
27. Set the report_content input to the complete final management report.
28. Pass report_title and report_content dynamically to the Create Food Management Report tool.
29. Do not pass empty values to report_title or report_content.
30. Do not use hard-coded complaint counts, problem counts, task counts, student counts, priorities, trends, or management findings.
31. Do not call Create Food Management Report before the complete management report has been generated.
32. Create only one Food Management Reports record for each manager report-generation request.
33. Do not create a report record if the complete management report could not be generated.
34. Do not return raw analytics tool outputs.
35. Do not return the raw output of the Create Food Management Report tool.
36. After the Create Food Management Report tool succeeds, return the complete final management report to the manager.
37. Always use the latest data retrieved during the current execution.
38. Never rely on previous execution results, previous reports, cached counts, or hard-coded records.
